issues.failure_explanation:
The sentence infers, from the inequality in \eqref{eq:sobolev-norm-ineq-cyl}, that the operator-norm weighted Sobolev norm is finite for every cylindrical map with $C^k$ generator. The inequality only transfers finiteness from the weighted norm of the finite-dimensional generator $f^{N,N'}$, which is unrestricted for $C^k_{Cyl}$ maps (Definition def:cyl_map imposes only $f\in C^k$, no growth/integrability). Counterexample: $X=Y=\mathbb R$, $\mathcal E^X=\mathcal D^Y=I$, $f(y)=e^{y^2}\in C^\infty$, so $F(x)=e^{x^2}$; then $\int_{\mathbb R}|F'(x)|^p d
u(x)=\int |2xe^{x^2}|^p d
u=\infty$ for the finite Gaussian measure $
u$, hence $\|F\|_{\mathcal W^{k,p}_
u(\mathbb R,\mathbb R)}=\infty$. The finiteness holds only for the subclass $C^{k;p}_{
u,Cyl}$, which is exactly the class defined (with the finiteness condition made explicit) immediately before this sentence and used in all theorems.

failure_location.quote: $\|F^{{\mathcal E}^X,{\mathcal D}^Y}\|_{\mathcal W^{k,p}_{ \nu}(X,Y)}<\infty,$ for all $  F^{{\mathcal E}^X,{\mathcal D}^Y}\in C^k_{Cyl}(X,Y).$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the claim with the quantifier restricted to $F^{{\mathcal E}^X,{\mathcal D}^Y}\in C^{k;p}_{\nu,Cyl}(X,Y)$, or add the hypothesis $\|f^{N,N'}\|_{\mathcal W^{k,p}_{\nu^{\mathcal E^X}}(\mathbb R^N,\mathbb R^{N'})}<\infty$; this is exactly how the class is used afterwards.
issues.overall_effect: The false sentence suggests that all of $C^k_{Cyl}(X,Y)$ lies in the weighted Sobolev ambient spaces; a reader relying on it would treat cylindrical approximants as automatically $\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal W^{k,p}_\nu}$-finite. No labelled definition, theorem, or proof uses this claim (they all use $C^{k;p}_{\mu^0,Cyl}(X,Y)$, whose finiteness condition is explicit), so the damage is confined to this assertion.
issues.title: Weighted Sobolev norm claimed finite for every C^k cylindrical map
issues.why_classification: Deleting or qualifying one inline sentence preserves every definition, theorem, and guarantee; no labelled result or downstream argument relies on the false finiteness claim, so the repair is local with no mathematical loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, the definition is extended by induction for $k\in \mathbb N$, i.e. $D^{k,p}_{\gamma}(X,Y):=\{F\in D^{k-1,p}_{\gamma}(X,Y): D_{\gamma}F\in D^{k-1,p}_{\gamma}(X,\mathcal L_2(X_{\gamma},Y)\}$
Moreover, using the fundamental theorem of calculus, if $F\in C_B^1(X,Y)$ then we have that it is ray absolutely continuous.  Hence, the case $k=1$ follows.

We say that $F: X \rightarrow Y$ is $C^1_B$ (i.e. in the sense of Bastiani, from which the subscript ``B'') on $X$ if it has Gâteaux derivative at any $x\in X$  and  $DF(\cdot)(\cdot) \in C^0(X \times X; Y)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs the inclusion $C^{k;p,2}_{B,\gamma,\eta}(X,Y)\subset D^{k,p}_{\gamma}(X,Y)$ for arbitrary $k$. By the paper's own recollection of Bogachev's definitions, $D^{k,p}_\gamma$-membership requires, iteratively, that $x\mapsto D_\gamma F(x)$ (and the higher iterates) be stochastically Gâteaux differentiable as an $\mathcal L_2(X_\gamma,Y)$-valued map (difference quotients converging in the Hilbert-Schmidt norm, at least in measure) and ray absolutely continuous. The argument given proves only: Bochner measurability of $D_\gamma F$ via the continuous finite-rank truncations $G^N$, ray absolute continuity of the $Y$-valued map $F$, and pointwise Gâteaux differentiability. Bastiani joint continuity of $(x,h)\mapsto D^2F(x)(h_1,h_2)$ gives, for each fixed $u$, continuity of the difference quotients $t\mapsto D^2F(x+th)(\iota u,\iota h)$, but no uniformity in $u$ over the Cameron-Martin ball; hence convergence of the Hilbert-Schmidt norms of the $\mathcal L_2(X_\gamma,Y)$-valued difference quotients of $D_\gamma F$ (needed for stochastic differentiability of $D_\gamma F$, and a fortiori for the higher iterates) is never established. 'Iterating the argument' is therefore not a valid inference: the properties proved for the $Y$-valued map $F$ do not transfer to the $\mathcal L_2$-valued derivative maps. The claimed equalities \eqref{eq:gaussian_sobolev_characterization}, \eqref{eq:gaussian_sobolev_characterization_p=2} and \eqref{eq:A=ambient_gauss} are consequently unsupported for $k\ge 2$.

failure_location.quote: According to definitions of spaces $D_{\gamma}^{k,p}(X,Y)$ in \cite{bogachev1998gaussian}, we iterate the argument to have the claim for arbitrary $k$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the missing containment $C^{k;p,2}_{B,\gamma,\eta}(X,Y)\subset D^{k,p}_\gamma(X,Y)$ by induction: for $F\in C^k_B$ with finite Gaussian HS-Sobolev norms, show (i) Borel/Bochner measurability of the iterated Cameron-Martin derivatives as $\mathcal L^i_2$-valued maps via finite-rank truncations; (ii) convergence in measure (indeed in $L^p(\gamma)$) of the HS-valued difference quotients of $D^{i-1}_\gamma F$ along Cameron-Martin directions, using the fundamental theorem of calculus along rays, truncation in the Cameron-Martin basis, and dominated/uniform-integrability arguments based on the finite moments $\int\|D^i_\gamma F\|^p_{HS}d\gamma<\infty$ together with Cameron-Martin quasi-invariance; and (iii) ray absolute continuity of these HS-valued maps. This contained lemma then validates the chain \eqref{eq:inclusions_gaussian_proof} and all the displayed identifications.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's headline consistency claim - that the newly constructed spaces recover the classical Gaussian Sobolev spaces of Bogachev (used in the abstract, in 'Recovering classical Gaussian Sobolev spaces', and relied on to justify Corollary th:UA_gaussian's route through Theorem th:characterization_bogachev and Remark rem:bogachev_charact_banach) - is unproved for $k\ge2$. The universal approximation results themselves are unaffected: Theorem th:UAT_Sobolev_Banach does not use this theorem, and Corollary th:UA_gaussian admits a direct proof from Assumption ass:finite_dim_sobolev_approx and the completion definition \eqref{eq:gaussian_sobolev} without the contested inclusion.
issues.title: Gaussian Sobolev identification (Theorem th:characterization_bogachev) unproved for k >= 2: iterated stochastic differentiability in Hilbert-Schmidt topology never established
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a genuinely nontrivial (though contained and standard-type) inductive argument on stochastic differentiability in Hilbert-Schmidt topology, so the issue exceeds 'minor'; however the theorem's statement appears salvageable without new global architecture (all needed inputs - joint continuity, HS moment bounds from membership in the space, Gaussian quasi-invariance - are available), no universal approximation result depends on it, and no advertised approximation guarantee is lost, so the loss is limited and the classification is moderate rather than serious.
